outcome: Pregnancy outcomes (live birth, fetal death, spontaneous abortion, pregnancy termination)
Mode of delivery (cesarean, operative vaginal, spontaneous vaginal)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, admission to NICU)
cohort: 24 women with a Fontan palliation who delivered at UCLA Medical Center
finding: While women with Fontan circulation can have successful pregnancies, they are at increased risk for cardiac complications, preterm delivery, and small-for-gestational-age neonates, likely due to impaired increases in cardiac output during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Of the live births, 53% were delivered via cesarean section, 28% by operative vaginal delivery, and 20% by spontaneous vaginal delivery.
birth_weight: 40% of neonates were born small (<10th percentile) for gestational age
